plan.title: AD lesional vs control DE + hallmark GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a single gene-symbol count matrix from Salmon (12,000 genes x 12 samples, counts.csv) with a 12-row metadata table giving one condition column: 6 atopic-dermatitis lesional skin vs 6 control, unpaired, one batch. The research question has two parts — which genes change, and which hallmark pathways change — plus one explicit data concern: sample_01 has a library size roughly 4x below the median.

The depth concern is handled first and explicitly rather than by deletion (T1S1). DESeq2's median-of-ratios size factors already absorb a depth difference as an offset inside the negative-binomial model, so a shallow library gives wider intervals, not biased fold changes. The plan therefore keeps sample_01 through blind-VST PCA (top 500 variable genes) and a sample-distance heatmap, reports its library size and detected-gene count beside the other eleven, and only removes it if it fails on structure — not on depth. Because the decision is a judgement, T1S2 runs the primary DESeq2 Wald test on all 12 samples and repeats it with sample_01 excluded as a sensitivity analysis, reporting how the DE gene set moves; that turns the caveat into a measured quantity instead of an assumption.

T1S2 does the modelling: minimal pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=6 samples, the smallest group size), ~condition with control set as the explicit reference so a positive log2FC means higher in lesional, Wald test, apeglm shrinkage for reporting and ranking, BH with independent filtering at alpha 0.05, and a p-value histogram inspected before the adjustment is trusted. With 6 per group DESeq2 flags Cook's-distance count outliers and returns NA p-values rather than replacing counts, so the NA classes are reported separately. T1S2b adds an edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test on the identical filtered matrix and design; the intersection with the DESeq2 calls is the high-confidence set, which matters at n=6 with one shallow library.

T2S1 answers the pathway half. Enrichment runs as preranked fgsea on the full list of tested genes — no threshold cut — ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic (the disputed choice is made explicitly: the Wald stat scales effect by its uncertainty, which is what a shallow-library dataset needs, and it avoids both the noisy unshrunken LFC and p-value ties). MSigDB human hallmark (2026.1, 50 sets, HGNC symbols) is present in the reference store and matches the gene-symbol identifier space of counts.csv directly, so hallmark GSEA needs no ID conversion. GO BP (also staged, human) is the second collection for mechanism-level follow-up; Reactome C2 is not staged, and that substitution is stated in the report. Sets are intersected with tested genes and kept at 15-500 members, redundant significant sets collapsed, leading-edge genes listed.

T1S3 assembles the report: MA and dispersion plots, the gene table with unshrunken LFC, shrunken LFC and lfcSE, DESeq2/edgeR overlap, the sample_01 sensitivity comparison, the enrichment provenance (collection, version, rank metric, universe, size window, seed), and sessionInfo.

The number of significant genes from DESeq2, from edgeR, and the size of the intersection are all reported
Genes called by only one method are listed as a secondary set labelled with the calling method
The union is not presented as the primary DE result
constraints: Use the same filtered matrix and the same design as T1S2 — do not re-filter differently
Use the quasi-likelihood F-test (glmQLFit + glmQLFTest), not the classic exact test
Treat the DESeq2/edgeR intersection as the high-confidence set
caveats: Disagreement between the two tools grows at low counts and low replicate numbers; a large method-specific set is informative, not a bug to hide

grounding.reason: edgeR quasi-likelihood is the listed alternative and the second method for the robustness check at 2-11 replicates per group (R-0001@9a17); the intersection is the high-confidence set per R-0042@54e1.

steps.name: Preranked hallmark GSEA on the Wald statistic
steps.question: Which MSigDB hallmark pathways are coordinately up or down in AD lesional skin relative to control, and which genes form the leading edge of each?
steps.description: Take the full T1S2 results table for every tested gene — no significance cut — and rank genes by the DESeq2 Wald statistic (the stat column), descending. Run fgsea against the MSigDB human hallmark collection (50 HALLMARK_* sets, HGNC symbols, 2026.1 release), intersecting each set with the tested genes and keeping sets with 15 to 500 members after the intersection. Adjust with BH and set an explicit random seed for the permutations. Collapse significant sets that share most of their leading-edge genes and report one representative per group, keeping the full table as a supplement. List the leading-edge genes of each significant set with each gene's Wald statistic and shrunken log2FoldChange, and mark leading-edge overlap between reported sets. Then repeat the same preranked run against the human GO Biological Process collection as the mechanism-level second pass, and report how many hallmark hits are corroborated there.
steps.context: The reference store holds MSigDB human hallmark 2026.1 (50 sets, HGNC gene symbols) and MSigDB human GO BP/CC/MF 2026.1. counts.csv is keyed on gene symbols, so the ranked list is already in the collection's identifier space and no Entrez conversion is needed — report the share of ranked genes that fail to match any hallmark set as the unmapped fraction. The Reactome C2 subset that would normally be the second collection for human data is NOT staged in this environment; GO BP is used in its place and this substitution must be stated in the output. If hallmark is unexpectedly absent at run time, report the absence explicitly and fall back to GO BP alone rather than substituting silently.
acceptance_criteria: fgsea runs on the FULL ranked list of tested genes from T1S2 — the list is not thresholded by padj or fold change before the test
The ranking metric is the DESeq2 Wald statistic (stat), and this choice is stated in the output alongside the reason
Gene sets are intersected with the tested genes and filtered to 15-500 members; the number of hallmark sets surviving the window is reported
The gene set collection name and version (MSigDB human hallmark 2026.1) and the random seed are recorded in the output
Significant hallmark sets at BH-adjusted p < 0.05 are reported with NES, adjusted p-value, set size and leading-edge gene list
Redundant significant sets are collapsed to representatives, with the full table kept as a supplement
The share of ranked genes not matching any set in the collection is reported
The GO BP second pass runs on the same ranked list and the substitution of GO BP for the unavailable Reactome C2 collection is stated explicitly
constraints: enrichment: gsea_input = full_ranked_list — never cut the list at padj or fold change before the test

enrichment: rank_metric = stat (DESeq2 Wald statistic). Disputed rule R-0108: this plan chooses the Wald statistic because it scales the effect by its uncertainty, which matters with one shallow library; the unshrunken log2FC alone and a signed p-value with ties are both rejected
enrichment: min_size = 15, max_size = 500, applied after intersecting each set with the tested genes
enrichment: universe = tested genes from T1S2, not the whole genome or the whole annotation
enrichment: collapse_redundant = true — collapse overlapping significant sets and report one representative each
enrichment: primary collection is the human MSigDB hallmark gene sets (symbols); resolve it from the reference store and record its version
enrichment: report the unmapped share of the ranked list
Set and record an explicit random seed for the fgsea permutations
caveats: If fewer than about 50 genes pass the significance threshold in T1S2, do not run an over-representation test on that short list — the preranked method on the full ranked list is the correct and only enrichment here. State the size of the significant list in the report
Enrichment results depend on the method: present each significant set as a hypothesis for follow-up, not as a proven mechanism
Gene length and expression level bias enrichment on count data; using the tested genes as the universe removes only the detection part of that bias
Reactome C2 is not staged in this environment — GO BP substitutes as the second collection and the substitution must be named in the output, not glossed over

grounding.reason: Human ranked-list enrichment after DE: fgsea preranked on the full tested list against MSigDB Hallmark per R-0107@976c and R-0048@500d; disputed rank metric R-0108@409f resolved in favour of the Wald statistic per R-0099@0a77. Reactome (R-0098@d01b) is not staged, so GO BP is the stated second collection.

steps.name: Consolidated results and reproducibility report
steps.question: What is the defensible answer to which genes and which hallmark pathways change between AD lesional and control skin, and what are the limits of that answer given n=6 per group and one shallow library?
steps.description: Assemble the final report from T1S1, T1S2, T1S2b and T2S1. Include: the MA plot and the dispersion plot as the two fit diagnostics, placed before the gene tables; the gene table with baseMean, unshrunken log2FoldChange, apeglm-shrunken log2FoldChange and lfcSE, ranked by the shrunken value and with the shrinkage estimator named in the header; the DESeq2/edgeR significant counts and their intersection as the high-confidence set; the sample_01 sensitivity comparison and the keep/drop decision with its reason; the hallmark GSEA table with NES, adjusted p and leading-edge genes per significant set, marking leading-edge overlap between sets; and the enrichment provenance (collection name, version, rank metric, universe, size window, tool version, multiple-testing method, seed). State the design formula, the contrast, the thresholds, the number of genes tested after filtering, and the number of DE genes. Attach sessionInfo with every package version. State plainly the method-dependence of the enrichment result and the power limits of a 6 vs 6 unpaired design.
steps.context: This is the synthesis the user reads. Its job is to make the DE and pathway answers usable and to state their limits without softening them — particularly the modest replicate number, the single shallow library, and the fact that pathway hits are hypotheses.
acceptance_criteria: The MA plot and the dispersion plot both appear before the gene tables, each with a one-line statement of what it shows
The gene table carries the unshrunken log2FoldChange, the apeglm-shrunken log2FoldChange and lfcSE, and genes are ranked by the shrunken value with the estimator named
Method, package versions, design formula, contrast (lesional vs control), thresholds, number of genes tested after filtering and number of DE genes are all stated
The DESeq2/edgeR intersection is presented as the high-confidence gene set with its size
The sample_01 keep/drop decision, its stated reason, and the sensitivity-fit overlap are reported
Leading-edge genes are listed per significant gene set, with overlap between reported sets marked
Enrichment provenance is complete: collection, version, rank metric, universe, size window, tool version, adjustment method, seed
sessionInfo and the random seeds are stored with the results
The report states the method-dependence of the enrichment result and does not present a pathway hit as a proven mechanism
constraints: Rank genes and draw plots on the shrunken log2 fold change; keep the unshrunken estimate and the p-values from the unshrunken fit in the table
Report the number of significant genes from DESeq2 and from edgeR and the size of the intersection; do not present the union as the result
State the enrichment collection, version, rank metric, universe and size window
Record sessionInfo, package versions, the fgsea seed, and the gene set collection version with the results, not in a separate note
State that enrichment results depend on the method chosen
caveats: Do not overstate: 6 vs 6 unpaired with one ~4x shallow library is a modest design; report effect sizes and interval widths rather than implying precision the data does not carry
If the DE gene count is small, say so plainly instead of relaxing the threshold to produce a longer list

grounding.reason: Report content follows the returned report-step rules: MA and dispersion diagnostics (R-0087@c53d), shrunken plus unshrunken effect columns (R-0085@c24d), two-method overlap (R-0042@54e1), leading edge per set (R-0105@c4a8), and the full reproducibility record (R-0086@becf, R-0041@059a, R-0051@01ca).
